parsed.explanation: Combined operative regime: the division's protections (public-accommodation coverage, enhanced bias-crime penalties, a ban on gay/trans panic defences, surgery-free marker changes, documented care protection for travellers) are real but do not govern entry, federal facilities or federal custody. Those layers remain national: visitor entry refusal on document discrepancy with a possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, a federal rule barring congruent access to government-funded single-sex facilities, documented immigration-custody abuse of trans men, and national subpoenas of minors' hospital records. Litigation is unresolved. The division's low recorded violence and lack of documented state-level exposure offset some of this, but the national exposures set the operative floor, placing the case in the Elevated Risk band.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport sex-marker restriction in effect after November 2025 ruling. Cable instructs refusal where documents or other evidence cast doubt on sex, with a possible permanent fraud ineligibility finding. Athlete entry ban announced February 2025.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, and has limited waivers. Passport restrictions are under challenge in national courts.
entry_documents.interaction: Division marker liberalisation governs only state documents and cannot affect the national entry screen a visitor passes through.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reportedly involved forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men. National corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies from 2026 and stopped reporting trans prisoner counts.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented for the division's own custody practice. National orders on prison LGBTQ rights were rescinded.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Federal detention after a document discrepancy bypasses the division's protective statutes entirely.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with gender identity, reaching federal buildings and federal custody nationwide.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division public-accommodation law covers transportation and facilities-related denials. Some national orders have been enjoined. Division facilities rules are not documented as restrictive, but the map notes other sex-defining laws may still affect access.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility rules operate inside the division and are not overridden by its accommodation law.

care_services.exposure: Summer 2025 federal subpoena of over 20 hospitals for full records of patients under 19. Proposed federal rule to bar public reimbursement of care under 18. National youth crisis lifeline services closed.
care_services.protection: Division April 2023 order protects gender-affirming care, including for people travelling in from other jurisdictions. Division bans conversion efforts directed at minors.
care_services.interaction: A minor receiving care in the division may generate federal records. The division order does not address out-of-state subpoenas, and their effect is not described.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: December 2025 federal reward system references 'radical gender ideology'. May 2026 counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for neutralisation. January 2025 order directs prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism strategy states powers will not target people who simply disagree. Division has enhanced bias-crime penalties and a 2020 ban on gay/trans panic defences.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National threat framing applies to every resident and visitor regardless of division protections, and the division's protective laws do not reach federal investigative action.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor's documents may trigger the entry discrepancy route. Federal subpoena and reimbursement exposure applies to under-19 care. Three division school boards adopted parental-notification policies in 2023 that outed trans students; the outcome of the challenge is unsourced.
minors_guardians.protection: Division school guidance supports names, pronouns and facility use by gender identity. The interscholastic athletic association permits participation by gender identity. Division bans conversion efforts for minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor enrolled at a school in a board with an outing policy could be exposed. Parent-guardian exposure runs through the care-subpoena and entry-screen routes.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific trans violence documented. A 2026 dataset places the division among the safest measured per-capita rates for killings of trans women. The documented trespass arrest, handcuffing and 24 hours in a men's ward occurred in a different unit and is not attributed to the division.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Enhanced bias-crime penalties where bias rests on gender identity. Public-accommodation enforcement body can grant relief.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Whether bias-crime enhancements have been applied to trans victims is not documented, so the protection's operation is uncertain.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No complaint or prosecution statistics for the division's gender-identity anti-discrimination provisions. Federal challenges unresolved. Effect of out-of-state records demands on division providers not described. Division school policy status unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Division civil-rights body can investigate and grant relief. Same-sex marriage recognised here and nationally. Document openness is resident-facing and treated as climate only.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Division remedies do not reach federal entry or custody. Absence of enforcement data is not evidence of safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: The 0.25-C anchor has birth-sex housing with frequent assaults, a cross-dressing arrest statute and solitary used as protection. This dossier lacks a division-level housing or arrest statute, so it sits higher. Federal immigration-custody abuse is comparable in kind, which keeps the case in the same general exposure tier for anyone detained federally.

The 0.45-D anchor has universal registration and nightly hotel data sharing, making exposure durable for every visitor. This dossier documents no comparable visitor registry; its entry exposure is discretionary refusal on discrepancy. Division protections push it above the anchor, while the federal custody record keeps it near it.

The 0.65-E anchor has birth-sex questioning, but appeals succeed, detention is barred by policy and remedies operate. This dossier has no documented working federal remedy for entry or custody harms, and national litigation is unresolved, so it sits materially lower.

The 0.75-D anchor has protective enforcement, working police review and prosecution of attackers. The division approaches that tier on local protections, but federal entry refusal, federal custody abuse and federal facility exclusion are unresolved in this dossier. Reaching 0.75 would require national entry and custody protections in operation.

parsed.synthesis: A visitor's exposure runs through the national layer regardless of the division's protections. Entry screening can refuse a visitor whose documents conflict with sex, with a rare permanent fraud finding. Federal immigration custody carries documented severe abuse, and federal subpoenas can reach records of minors receiving care. The division's accommodation, bias-crime, care and marriage protections, plus its low recorded violence, lift the case above the national floor. Those protections do not reach federal checkpoints or custody, so the operative regime remains elevated-risk. Minors add records-subpoena and school-policy exposure. Litigation outcomes and out-of-state crossings could move the rating.
